Standardize an Epoch Length

Source: R/acti_standardize_epoch.R
acti_standardize_epoch.Rd

Converts an epoch given as a number, a string such as "1 min", "30s", "5 seconds", or "1 hour", a lubridate Duration or Period, or a difftime into a consistent representation: either a number in a given unit (e.g. 60 seconds) or a string that can be passed to lubridate::floor_date() (e.g. "1 min").

Usage

acti_standardize_epoch(
  epoch,
  unit = c("seconds", "minutes", "hours", "days", "auto"),
  output = c("numeric", "character"),
  input_unit = c("seconds", "minutes", "hours", "days")
)

acti_standardise_epoch(
  epoch,
  unit = c("seconds", "minutes", "hours", "days", "auto"),
  output = c("numeric", "character"),
  input_unit = c("seconds", "minutes", "hours", "days")
)

Arguments

epoch

A single epoch length: a positive number (in input_unit), a string parseable by lubridate::duration() ("1 min", "1min", "30s", "2 hours"; "hr" and the lubridate arbitrary units such as "90 aseconds" are also accepted), a Duration, a Period, or a difftime. Calendar units without a fixed length (months, quarters, years, ...) are not epochs and give an error.

unit

Unit to standardize the epoch to: one of "seconds", "minutes", "hours", "days", or "auto". "auto" is only available for output = "character" and picks the largest unit that lubridate::floor_date() can round with (e.g. "1 min" rather than "60 secs"), falling back to "aseconds" for lengths such as 90 seconds. Defaults to "seconds" for numeric output and "auto" for character output. Singular and abbreviated unit names are matched to the unit they name: "second", "sec", and "secs" are treated as "seconds"; "minute", "min", and "mins" as "minutes"; "hour", "hr", and "hrs" as "hours"; and "day" as "days". Other names, including partial ones such as "m", are an error.

output

Type of output: "numeric" returns the length in unit, "character" returns a string such as "30 secs", "1 min", or "2 hours", which lubridate::floor_date(), seq(), cut(), and MIMSunit all understand.

input_unit

Unit of epoch when epoch is numeric (or a string with no unit, such as "60"). Ignored otherwise. Abbreviations are matched as for unit.

Value

A numeric value or a single string.

Note

The "aseconds" fallback for output = "character" relies on the absolute-unit rounding that lubridate::floor_date() has supported since lubridate 1.9.0.

Examples

acti_standardize_epoch(60)
#> [1] 60
acti_standardize_epoch("1 min")
#> [1] 60
acti_standardize_epoch("1 min", unit = "minutes")
#> [1] 1
acti_standardize_epoch(30, output = "character")
#> [1] "30 secs"
acti_standardize_epoch(60, output = "character")
#> [1] "1 min"
acti_standardize_epoch(5, input_unit = "minutes")
#> [1] 300
acti_standardize_epoch("2 hours", unit = "minutes", output = "character")
#> [1] "120 mins"
acti_standardize_epoch(lubridate::minutes(5))
#> [1] 300
acti_standardize_epoch(as.difftime(30, units = "secs"), output = "character")
#> [1] "30 secs"
